title: Speak for Yourself with Clarity and Power
coreMove: Report your experience as discussable material without turning your interpretation into a verdict.
sourcePressure: The chapter teaches owned expression: observation, internal response, and the story you began telling, plus honesty calibration under reaction.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Generic assertiveness or softer accusations labeled as I-statements.

sourceAnchors.name: the story I started telling myself
sourceAnchors.detail: The source uses the story component to keep interpretation owned and checkable rather than hardened into accusation.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The same interpretation can open the door or lock it, depending on whether you offer it as a story or a verdict.

sourceAnchorsNote: No chapter-specific real named anecdote, study, or researcher was available in the source sidecars for this chapter. Source anchors are traceable framework artifacts or edition/context facts only; do not invent named studies or reuse the source-banned Jack-Michael, Sydney, or author-family examples.

hook: Do not open ch10 with a generic dread-before-meeting frame
Do not begin with a definition of the chapter term
Do not use a negotiation-table abstraction as the first image
counterintuition: Avoid the shell 'you think X, but actually Y'
Avoid claiming the idea is simply counterintuitive
Avoid treating compassion as the surprising twist
tryThisNow: No 'pause and reflect on your communication style' action
examples: Avoid repeated coffee-table, classroom, narrow-kitchen, bus-depot, marker, mug, or radiator shells
Avoid six workplace meetings with changed names
Avoid making every case a manager feedback scene

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: use these six opening devices in order: retrospective first line; second-person You direct address; sensory detail first; dialogue first line; environmental detail before any human; question-as-hook
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of timestamp plus named protagonist plus prop plus decision that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.stakes: a missed promotion list has started a story about invisibility
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Sophie names the announcement, the feeling, and the story without accusing Marit of ignoring her career
exampleSpecs.firstImage: an announcement email printed beside a marked-up resume

exampleSpecs.audience: friends who have minimized too long
exampleSpecs.stakes: a friendship will become brittle if the point keeps being underdone
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Marit says the honest version before she can bury it in jokes
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a sink full of wine glasses after everyone leaves

exampleSpecs.stakes: a critique that landed as dismissal could become a learning conversation
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Marco reports the exact sentence, the embarrassment, and the story it started
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "When you said 'that is basic,' I went quiet," he says

exampleSpecs.audience: civic professionals naming exclusion without motive claims
exampleSpecs.stakes: a public committee missed one department whose work is affected
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Ryan states the observable omission and the story he is checking before proposing any remedy
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a laminated seating chart in a council chamber

exampleSpecs.domain: designer responding to harsh client edits
exampleSpecs.stakes: a client relationship may survive if the feeling is serious but not inflated
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Chidi trims 'you destroyed the project' into the honest version of what happened for him
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a PDF covered with tracked edits

exampleSpecs.domain: adult child speaking to parent about old pattern
exampleSpecs.audience: families where the hard thing gets taken back
exampleSpecs.stakes: the parent's first flinch may tempt the adult child to erase the truth
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Olivier lets the reaction happen and keeps the statement available for discussion
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a kettle clicking off in a quiet kitchen

skillTargets: identify when a scenario needs report your experience as discussable material without turning your interpretation into a verdict.
distinguish speak from your own experience from the adjacent generic misread
choose the visible action that demonstrates the chapter move rather than merely naming it
explain why the wrong option would recreate generic assertiveness or softer accusations labeled as i-statements.

tryThisNowSpec: Turn one accusation into three owned parts: observable event, internal response, and the story you started telling yourself.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm - a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
